You are helping in a project that uses the Taproot design system. Its packages are installed in node_modules.

Build the page as one HTML file named index.html in the current directory, with Taproot's web components. There is no bundler: load what the page needs from node_modules. Write the components as markup in the HTML, not from script. When the file is written, reply with one line saying so.

Build an address form with a street address that can take several lines, a country chosen from about 200 countries (include five as a sample), and a required postal code. A Save address button submits it.
I need to explore the Taproot packages.

43	
44	## Forms
45	
46	Set `name` to include the current value in form submission. The `value` attribute supplies the
47	initial value; the `value` property changes the current value without changing the reset value.
48	A non-empty `error` blocks submission.
49	
50	To validate in your own code, set `novalidate` on the form so the submit reaches your listener.
51	Read the values there, and set `error` on each field that needs a correction. Clear `error` on the
52	field's `input` event and when the form resets, because a reset leaves it set.
53	
54	Provide native `<option>` children, optionally grouped by `<optgroup label="…">`.
55	The component copies this content into its shadow `<select>` and observes changes to choice text,
56	values, disabled states, and groups. Option event listeners are not copied. Use the component's
57	`input` and `change` events.
58	
59	An initial `value` attribute takes precedence over an option's `selected` attribute. Without
60	`value`, native option defaults determine the reset value. A first empty-valued option provides a
61	prompt and makes a required Select invalid until a non-empty value is chosen. The menu appearance
62	and opening keys follow the browser and operating system.

28	---
29	
30	## Forms
31	
32	Text field defaults to `type="text"`. Set `name` so the value is included when the form submits.
33	Pair it with Button to submit:
34	
35	```html
36	<form>
37	  <ds-text-field label="Email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required></ds-text-field>
38	  <ds-button type="submit">Continue</ds-button>
39	</form>
40	```
41	
42	A non-empty `error` marks the field invalid, associates that message with the control, and blocks
43	submit until the message is cleared. Use `hint` for guidance that is not an error.
44	
45	To validate in your own code, set `novalidate` on the form so the submit reaches your listener.
46	Read the values there, and set `error` on each field that needs a correction. Clear `error` on the
47	field's `input` event and when the form resets, because a reset leaves it set.
48	
49	The `value` attribute sets the initial value, which form reset restores. `autocomplete` takes the
50	HTML autofill tokens, such as `email` or `current-password`, so the browser can offer saved values.

38	---
39	
40	## Forms
41	
42	Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set the type when it participates in a form:
43	
44	```html
45	<form>
46	  <!-- form fields -->
47	  <ds-button type="button" variant="secondary">Cancel</ds-button>
48	  <ds-button type="submit" variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
49	</form>
50	```
51	
52	Use `type="reset"` only when restoring every form control to its initial value is the intended
53	behavior.
54	
55	## Styles
56	
57	Do not recreate Button states with product CSS. Use the published variants and sizes first. Treat
58	`::part(button)` as an escape hatch that requires a specific product need and design review.
59	
60	## Icons
61	
62	Mark a decorative icon hidden from assistive technology. Provide `aria-label` when an icon is the
63	only visible content.
64	
65	## Why `aria-label` and not `label`
66	
67	Button maps `accessibleName` to `aria-label`, while Icon, Spinner, and Tabs map it to `label`. The
68	difference is deliberate. `aria-label` is the attribute people already put on an icon-only button,
69	and Button only passes it to the native button inside, so it keeps its standard meaning. The other
70	three use `label` because their name does more than name: Icon is hidden from assistive technology
71	without one, Spinner falls back to "Loading", and Tabs names the tab list inside it rather than the
72	host. They set the name through `ElementInternals` or on that inner element, so the host never
73	gains `aria-*` attributes. Renaming either side would break published markup.

1	# @taproot-ds/tokens
2	
3	Design tokens for the Taproot design system — distributed as CSS custom properties and JSON. Built with [Style Dictionary](https://styledictionary.com).
4	
5	## Install
6	
7	```bash
8	pnpm add @taproot-ds/tokens
9	```
10	
11	## Quick start
12	
13	Link the single CSS file once at the root of your app. All token tiers are included.
14	
15	```html
16	<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
17	```
18	
19	Or import via a bundler:
20	
21	```js
22	import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
23	```
24	
25	Then use tokens in your CSS:
26	
27	```css
28	.card {
29	  background: var(--ds-semantic-color-background-surface);
30	  border: 1px solid var(--ds-semantic-color-border-default);
31	  color: var(--ds-semantic-color-foreground-default);
32	}
33	
34	.btn-primary {
35	  background: var(--ds-semantic-color-background-action-primary-default);
36	  color: var(--ds-semantic-color-foreground-on-action-primary);
37	  border-radius: var(--ds-semantic-radius-control);
38	}
39	```
40	
41	## Fonts
42	
43	The design system uses three typefaces, each mapped to a font token:
44	
45	| Token                          | Family         | Role                             |
46	| ------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
47	| `--ds-primitives-font-display` | Lora           | Headings, card titles, logotype  |
48	| `--ds-primitives-font-sans`    | Source Sans 3  | Body text, UI labels, buttons    |
49	| `--ds-primitives-font-mono`    | JetBrains Mono | Code, token values, numeric data |
50	
51	Each token includes a system fallback stack, so the UI remains readable if Google Fonts fails to load. To use the intended typefaces, add the following `<link>` tags to your document `<head>` **before** the tokens stylesheet:
52	
53	```html
54	<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
55	<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
56	<link
57	  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lora:ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@300..900&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap"
58	  rel="stylesheet"
59	/>
60	```
61	
62	The `display=swap` parameter ensures text renders immediately in the fallback font while the custom fonts load, avoiding invisible text during page load.
63	
64	If you are using a bundler with a `<head>` injection plugin (e.g. Vite's `vite-plugin-html`) or a framework like Next.js, load the fonts using your framework's preferred font mechanism instead of a raw `<link>` tag.
65	
66	## Token architecture
67	
68	Primitive and semantic tokens are the whole public vocabulary. Components read semantic tokens
69	directly; there is no component tier.
70	
71	```
72	Primitives  →  Semantic
73	  (scale)       (intent)
74	```
75	
76	| Tier          | Prefix              | Use when                                            |
77	| ------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
78	| **Primitive** | `--ds-primitives-*` | No semantic role expresses the raw scale choice     |
79	| **Semantic**  | `--ds-semantic-*`   | Styling components and product interfaces by intent |
80	
81	Color primitives are not published as CSS variables. Use a semantic color token, which follows the
82	active theme. The palette is still in `primitives.json` for design tooling.
83	
84	### Semantic token groups
85	
86	| Group                       | Example                                                 | Purpose                                 |
87	| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
88	| `background`                | `--ds-semantic-color-background-default`                | Page and surface fills                  |
89	| `foreground`                | `--ds-semantic-color-foreground-muted`                  | Text and icon colors                    |
90	| `border`                    | `--ds-semantic-color-border-default`                    | Dividers and outlines                   |
91	| `background.action.primary` | `--ds-semantic-color-background-action-primary-default` | Primary interactions                    |
92	| `background.brand`          | `--ds-semantic-color-background-brand-muted`            | Brand surfaces                          |
93	| `foreground.on`             | `--ds-semantic-color-foreground-on-action-primary`      | Content paired with a specific fill     |
94	| `*.status.*`                | `--ds-semantic-color-background-status-success-default` | Feedback surfaces, content, and borders |
95	
96	## Theming
97	
98	With no `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`, semantic tokens follow the user's system preference. A
99	dark system preference activates the dark theme through `prefers-color-scheme`; light is the
100	default.
101	
102	Set `data-theme` to override the system preference. The attribute always takes priority.
103	
104	```html
105	<html data-theme="light"></html>
106	<html data-theme="dark"></html>
107	```
108	
109	```js
110	document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
111	document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
112	document.documentElement.removeAttribute("data-theme"); // follow the system preference
113	```
114	
115	When the attribute is absent, changes to the system preference apply without JavaScript or a page
116	refresh. The stylesheet also sets `color-scheme`, so supported browser controls and scrollbars
117	match the active theme.
118	
119	A surface that must keep one appearance in both themes needs a semantic role for it. Propose one rather than hard-coding palette values.
120	
121	## JSON tokens
122	
123	Resolved token values are also available as JSON for use in design tooling, style pipelines, or non-CSS targets.
124	
125	```js
126	import primitives from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/primitives";
127	import semantic from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-light";
128	```
129	
130	The semantic tier is theme-specific. Import the semantic file that matches the
131	theme whose resolved values you need.
132	
133	```js
134	import semantic from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-dark";
135	```
136	
137	Descriptions are theme-independent. Import the meta file to read every semantic token's type and purpose. `description` is the token's own purpose, or null when none has been written. `groupDescription` is the purpose of a parent group, used by typography recipes, or null when the token has no described group.
138	
139	```js
140	import semanticMeta from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-meta";
141	```
142	
143	The CSS build needs no such split: `dist/css/tokens.css` carries both themes and swaps at runtime.
144	
145	## Build outputs
146	
147	| File                              | Contents                                                                    |
148	| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
149	| `dist/css/tokens.css`             | Primitives except color, and semantic light/dark. The package's main entry. |
150	| `dist/tokens/primitives.json`     | Raw primitive scale values, including the color palette                     |
151	| `dist/tokens/semantic.light.json` | Resolved semantic tokens for light theme                                    |
152	| `dist/tokens/semantic.dark.json`  | Resolved semantic tokens for dark theme                                     |
153	| `dist/tokens/semantic.meta.json`  | Type and purpose for every semantic token                                   |
154	
155	## Building from source
156	
157	From the repository root:
158	
159	```bash
160	pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@taproot-ds/tokens
161	```
162	
163	Source tokens live in `src/tokens/`. Never edit `dist/` files directly — they are regenerated on every build.
